requirement: Render the supplied Helm chart with the provided values. When service-account creation is enabled, the rendered resources must include the requested ServiceAccount and preserve its requested annotation and token-automount setting; the workload pod must use that same ServiceAccount name and token-automount setting. When creation is disabled, do not render the requested ServiceAccount and do not bind the workload to it.

When the v4.13.4 NFS CSI chart renders the configured VolumeSnapshotClass, preserve the supplied annotations on that object's metadata. When creation is disabled, do not render the VolumeSnapshotClass. Preserve unrelated chart output.

Render the supplied Helm chart with each provided values file. When migrationJob.enabled is true, the rendered migration Job must include the configured pod security context: runAsUser 1234, runAsGroup 1234, runAsNonRoot true, and seccompProfile.type RuntimeDefault. When migrations are disabled, no migration Job should be rendered. Preserve these input settings in the generated Kubernetes manifests.

Render the supplied chart for each values file. The storagesvc ServiceAccount must receive both the chart-wide workload-identity annotation and owner label, together with the storagesvc-specific role ARN. When serviceAccounts metadata is empty, retain the storagesvc ServiceAccount but emit none of those custom metadata fields.

Update the supplied Helm chart so that when the built-in Redis workload is enabled, the rendered Redis Deployment carries the configured global pod-level security context on its PodSpec and the configured global container security context on its Redis container, consistently with the chart's other workload deployments. Preserve the chart's existing behavior for unrelated resources. When built-in Redis is disabled and an external Redis URL is configured, do not render the built-in Redis Deployment.

When the ERun backend API chart creates dedicated ServiceAccounts for the API and env-deployer Job, propagate the supplied imagePullSecrets list to both accounts. When imagePullSecrets is omitted, leave the field absent on both accounts. Preserve unrelated rendered resources.
KAI Scheduler global.imagePullSecrets entries must render as secret names in kai-config and propagate to the crd-upgrader Job pod spec.
When the metrics dashboard is enabled, propagate global.imagePullSecrets into the rendered dashboard Deployment pod spec. Preserve normal chart behavior when the global secret list is empty.
Values supplied in jobs[].securityContext must propagate to the generated Job pod and container security contexts.

When rendering the chart's server test Pod, propagate the configured server pod and container securityContext fields into the Pod template. Preserve explicitly supplied values, including alternate values, in the rendered Pod. When the server is disabled, no server test Pod should be rendered.

When the llm-gateway chart renders gateway, admin UI, and admin API Ingresses, propagate each ingress component's configured annotations to that specific resource. Preserve shared annotations and unrelated chart output.

When rendering the chart with standalone mode enabled, propagate any supplied podAnnotations to the standalone Deployment pod template metadata. If no annotations are supplied, leave that optional field absent. Preserve the rendered Deployment and unrelated chart output in both cases.
When the Brewet BFF component is enabled, its configured ServiceAccount name and annotations must reach the BFF ServiceAccount and the BFF Deployment must bind to that same account.

When config.run_interval is empty, render the scheduled CronJob branch and propagate imagePullSecrets into spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec. Preserve normal Deployment branch behavior when config.run_interval is set.

When rendering the API and web Deployments, propagate the configured imagePullSecrets to both pod specs. If no global imagePullSecrets are configured, leave them absent from both. Preserve unrelated chart output.

When the relay workload and ServiceAccount creation are enabled, the rendered relay Deployment must reference a ServiceAccount that the same chart render creates. When the relay workload and ServiceAccount creation are disabled, neither relay resource should be rendered. Preserve unrelated chart output.

When a node selector is configured for the chart, all generated hook Jobs must carry that selector in their pod template. When no selector is configured, the chart must not impose an effective node placement constraint.

When goldenUploader is enabled and top-level tolerations are supplied, render the exact toleration entry on its generated DaemonSet pod spec. When goldenUploader is disabled, do not render a golden-uploader DaemonSet. Preserve unrelated chart output.

When rendering the WireMock Deployment, propagate configured deployment annotations to the generated Deployment metadata. If the optional annotations field is absent, omit the metadata annotations block.

When livenessProbe values are supplied, render those exact values on the generated OpenSearch StatefulSet container. When livenessProbe is omitted, leave the StatefulSet container without a livenessProbe field. Preserve unrelated chart output in both cases.

Render the supplied chart with each provided values file. When a provider is declared, the generated ConfigMap config.toml must preserve the endpoint, emit threaded_replies and dry_run as TOML booleans, and propagate retry_max, retry_wait_min, and retry_wait_max with their supplied values and types. When no provider is declared, the ConfigMap must still render without a provider block or retry fields.

The configured shared nodeSelector, tolerations, and node affinity must appear in every generated backend, frontend, MinIO, and PostgreSQL pod template. When all three optional scheduling values are empty, no scheduling constraint should be added by the chart.

When app.extraEnv supplies an environment variable, render that exact name/value in a generated Deployment container. When app.extraEnv is omitted, do not render the supplied variable. Preserve unrelated chart output in both cases.

When KubeVela renders the enabled cluster-gateway TLS secret create and patch Jobs, global nodeSelector, tolerations, and affinity values must appear in both generated Job pod specs. When multicluster is disabled, neither target Job should be emitted.

If a Teams webhook Secret reference is configured, the generated Deployment application's container must include that reference under envFrom.secretRef. With the optional reference empty, no Teams Secret reference should be emitted.

Configured app.extraEnv and OpenTelemetry service version, trace sampler, sampler argument, metrics exporter and logs exporter values must be represented by matching environment entries in the rendered Deployment container. Empty optional values and an empty extraEnv list must not produce those entries.

Render the supplied Helm chart with the provided component values. For each generated workload, preserve the configured service-account token automount setting. With automount disabled for the operator, metrics API server, and webhook components, each corresponding Deployment must render the setting as false. With automount enabled, each must render true.

Explicit HTTP add-on logging settings must be rendered into the operator, external scaler, interceptor, and kube-rbac-proxy container arguments. When those settings are omitted, the trigger-specific values must not be injected, and the proxy keeps its default verbosity.
When rbac.create is false, KEDA's rendered chart must contain no Role or RoleBinding objects. With rbac.create true, the operator Role and RoleBinding must still be rendered.

For the kube-state-metrics chart, render the Deployment under both supplied values files. With no custom HTTP headers configured, the generated liveness and readiness probes must omit the httpHeaders field. With the supplied explicit header configuration, both probes must preserve that header. Assess only the generated chart output described here.
